📰 General

Xcel Energy Shuts Down Power to Over 87,000 Customers Due to Extreme Fire Risk •

Xcel Energy initiated a planned power shutdown across six Colorado counties – Boulder, Clear Creek, Gilpin, Jefferson, Larimer, and Weld – impacting approximately 87,000 customers. The decision was prompted by extremely dangerous fire conditions across the region, according to the energy provider. Crews are working to restore power, but estimated restoration times have not yet been released. Officials are urging residents to take precautions due to the heightened fire risk.

🌍 World

Dressed as Santa, Group Robs Montreal Grocery Store for ‘Needy’ •

A group of individuals dressed in Santa Claus costumes and accompanied by masked elves conducted a robbery at a Montreal supermarket. The perpetrators filled bags with approximately $3,000 worth of groceries before fleeing the scene during the night. Following the incident, the group released a statement explaining their actions were intended to provide food to those in need. Police are currently investigating the robbery and attempting to identify the individuals involved.

🦅 US

Timeline Reveals Claudio Neves Valente’s Actions Leading Up to Boston Shootings •

Investigators have released a detailed timeline outlining Claudio Manuel Neves Valente’s movements in the days and hours preceding the shootings at Brown University and MIT. The timeline indicates Valente spent time at both institutions, observing classes and interacting with faculty and students. Evidence suggests he was seen taking notes and engaging in conversations with professors, including Dr. Robert P. Vitanza at Brown and Dr. Robert E. Gross at MIT. Following the shootings, Valente was observed attempting to flee the scene and was later found deceased.

💰 Business

Instacart to Refund Subscribers Following $60 Million FTC Settlement •

Instacart has reached a settlement with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) involving a $60 million refund for affected subscribers. The settlement stems from an FTC lawsuit alleging numerous unlawful business practices employed by the grocery delivery app. The FTC accused Instacart of misleading consumers about pricing and delivery fees. As part of the agreement, Instacart will provide refunds to subscribers who were impacted by these alleged practices. The terms of the settlement are still being finalized.

💻 Technology

Nintendo Shifts Strategy: Cheaper Cartridges Announced, Then Reconsidered •

Nintendo initially announced plans to offer cheaper physical game cartridges for the Switch 2, aiming to provide a more affordable alternative to the previously utilized Game-Key Cards. However, a developer indicated that game prices are still anticipated to increase by approximately $10 when transitioning to the new physical format. The move represents a change in Nintendo’s approach to distribution, potentially impacting game pricing and consumer choice. This shift follows a previous announcement regarding the cartridge plans.

🎭 Entertainment

Rob Reiner’s Final Projects Revealed Before Tragic Passing •

Rob Reiner, a celebrated director, producer, and actor, was reportedly involved in several upcoming projects at the time of his death. Details regarding these projects, including a potential sequel to “Spinal Tap” and a documentary about Stonehenge, were revealed by sources. A documentary exploring the construction of Stonehenge was in development, alongside a film adaptation of the novel “The Bear.” Reiner’s representative confirmed he was actively engaged in these projects prior to his passing alongside his wife, Michele Singer Reiner.

🏅 Sports

Puka Nacua’s Career Game Sparks Controversy After Stunning Seahawks Victory •

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua recorded a career-high performance, catching eight passes for 119 yards and a touchdown during Thursday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks. However, the game concluded with Nacua facing criticism following a late-game celebration deemed excessive by Seahawks players and coaches. The Rams ultimately secured a dramatic victory, turning around a significant first-half deficit. Following the game, the Seahawks expressed their displeasure with Nacua’s actions, highlighting the contentious nature of the contest.

🔬 Science

Scientists Develop Sustainable Wall Material From Dirt, Water, and Trash •

Researchers at RMIT University in Melbourne have developed a novel building material utilizing readily available resources – soil, water, and recycled cardboard. The team created a composite material with properties comparable to traditional concrete, offering a potential solution to the environmental impact of cement production. The material’s development addresses the significant carbon emissions associated with cement manufacturing, a major contributor to global pollution. Initial testing indicates the material’s durability and strength, suggesting a viable alternative for construction applications.

🩺 Health

Therapist Reveals 8 Practical Tips to Combat Constant Worry and Overwhelm •

A therapist has outlined eight strategies for managing anxiety, recognizing that excessive worry can negatively impact overall health. The recommendations include grounding techniques, such as connecting with one’s body, to help individuals regain control during periods of distress. The expert suggests incorporating mindfulness practices and focusing on the present moment as key components of anxiety management. Furthermore, the advice emphasizes the importance of establishing healthy routines and limiting exposure to stressors.
